newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ sends kiwi higher, further spike up expected.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ sends kiwi higher, further spike up expected.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar was sent scurrying upwards on Monday after the Reserve Bank said it wanted monetary conditions somewhat firmer.
The Kiwi was sent more than half a U.S. cent up -- to a high of US$0.6958, compared with 0.6890 before the RB comment.
It closed at 5.20 p.m. (0520 GMT) at 0.6939/46 while the Trade-Weighted Index ended at 67.91 against from its 67.65 opening.
"I think it will head higher. The bank has put a floor under the kiwi," said a Wellington bank chief dealer.
The RBNZ said monetary conditions were settling too far from the desired level and it wants them somewhat firmer.

Acting Chief Manager of the Reserve Bank's Financial Markets Department, Michael Reddell, said that overall monetary conditions appeared to be settling at levels somewhat too low to be consistent with the intended stance of monetary policy.
Another dealer said the market appeared to be short.
"I think we will have another spike."
He noted that the trend was down before the bank's statement and that may be resumed.
"They have put a real band on the kiwi and that may need defending at some time," the dealer said.

The Wellington bank chief dealer said the RBNZ may end up with a mix on monetary conditions it does not desire -- a higher currency and lower interest rates -- and to rectify that the bank may need to set an official cash rate as it is considering doing.
